Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years

medicine_groups.note: Count a systemic oral formulation, including an ingredient in a combination product. For aspirin, require a known oral route and documented anti-inflammatory use. Exclude low-dose antiplatelet aspirin and local preparations. Use quantities and directions to establish overlap with lithium. Exclude injections, suppositories and documented low-dose antiplatelet aspirin, including Cartia, Astrix or Cardiprin taken for that purpose. For a name used on several forms, check that the supply was oral.

rule_for_models: At age 65 or older, cite both supplies and any qualifying fact when systemic lithium for any indication overlaps with a Group B oral NSAID, excluding confirmed non-overlap, local preparations and low-dose antiplatelet aspirin. If use could qualify but age, overlap under unclear or as-needed directions, or aspirin dose or purpose is uncertain, report only a possible finding and ask about the missing details, daily oral anti-inflammatory use including over-the-counter products, and new tremor, vomiting or unsteadiness. When an oral NSAID is started during lithium treatment, keep the interaction finding, include any dose adjustment or individual monitoring plan, and cite any serum lithium result around day 5 to 7 or ask when monitoring was checked or planned if the record gives no monitoring evidence.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review concurrent lithium and oral NSAID use, whether another option for pain relief is suitable, and the plan for lithium levels and kidney function?

needs_facts.meets: Apply only to the aspirin branch. Count documented oral anti-inflammatory use. Exclude aspirin taken only for low-dose antiplatelet treatment or another confirmed use without an anti-inflammatory dose. Keep any separate qualifying oral NSAID in the review. If purpose or dose is unclear and anti-inflammatory use is plausible, report only a possible finding and ask why and how much the person takes.
